# Purpose and methods decisions

This application ports the requested analysis from `Analysis_unsup_strat.rmd`
in the former Yan project. It compares HiTME high-resolution immune-cell
compositions in Yan, Zhang and Bassez breast cancer, with Pelka colorectal
cancer providing a fourth cohort for feature harmonization and loading
correlations. The analysis uses precomputed annotations; it performs no gene
expression processing, annotation, batch correction or benchmark reruns.

**Application choices, distinct from the general benchmark:**

| Step | Rule used here |
|:--|:--|
| Upstream cohorts | Current configured benchmark-analysis inputs for Bassez/Zhang/Pelka; imported historical Yan annotations |
| Tissue selection | Zhang `Tissue == "tumor"`; Pelka `Tissue == "T"`; Bassez retains its configured Pre/treatment-naive/known-expansion selection |
| Annotation | HiTME **layer 2**, required explicitly; no fallback to broad or author labels |
| Eligible cells | Exact original exclusions listed below, including **neutrophils** |
| Sample cutoff | **At least 10 eligible immune cells**, before sparsity filtering/intersection; the old comment saying 50 was inaccurate |
| Sparse types | Remove a type when zero in **more than 90%** of retained samples within any cohort; exactly 90% is retained |
| Shared features | Intersection of filtered types across **all four cohorts**, including Pelka; no second sample cutoff after intersection |
| Zero handling | Add **0.5 to every count**, including positive counts and matrices without zeros; natural-log CLR |
| PCA | Separate centered, unscaled PCA in each cohort; all shared types, without HVCT selection |
| PCA orientation | Original lineage anchors for PC1/PC2; align other cohorts' PC2 loadings to Yan |
| Breast consensus bars | Original signed loadings from Yan/Zhang/Bassez, ordered by their three-cohort mean; Pelka does not enter the mean |
| Heatmaps | The same CLR as PCA, centered per cell type across samples, without variance scaling; Euclidean distances and Ward.D2 |

This retains the source's filtering while intentionally changing its PCA
pseudocount from **+1 to +0.5**, consistent with the ECODA benchmark's
`counts_all` convention and with these heatmaps. Current inputs can also differ
from the former packaged `example_data.rda`. Historical PDFs are visual
references, rather than expected numerical matches.

The exact excluded names are `Erythrocyte`, `Neutrophils`, `Platelet`,
`Endothelial`, `Epithelial`, `Fibroblast`, `abnormal cell`, `fibroblast`,
`perivascular cell`, and `endothelial cell`. Also exclude labels matching the
case-sensitive pattern `__|endo-|fibro-|VSMC-|peri-|CAFs|Unresolved`.
Consequently, “immune cells only” describes the original selected immune
compartment, **not every immune lineage**.

## Response annotations and separation from model fitting

Response labels are attached **after** composition preprocessing and PCA.
They never enter CLR, feature selection, PCA orientation or clustering.

- Yan: `pCR` → High; `RD` → Medium; literal `"NA"` → Low. The user confirmed
  that the last group represents early dropouts with the worst response.
  The supplementary table itself defines NA only as “not available”; the
  Low interpretation is therefore recorded as user-supplied clinical context.
  Actual R missing values remain missing.
- Zhang: PR/CR → High; SD → Medium; PD → Low.
- Bassez: E → High; NE → Low, representing the study's expansion endpoint.

These are study-specific endpoints, not identical clinical measures. Samples
with missing response remain in unsupervised analyses and are omitted only
from response comparisons. Boxplots retain the source's pairwise Wilcoxon
comparisons: asymptotic screening at p <= 0.05, then ggpubr's default Wilcoxon
labeling for those comparisons. Point jitter is horizontal and seeded for
reproducible display. Correlation-heatmap stars
are unadjusted two-sided Pearson tests across cell-type loadings, **not patient
scores**; no multiple-testing correction or confirmatory claim is added.

# Input provenance and preparation

The notebook runs from frozen compact local inputs. Preparation is explicit
and separate, and is not executed by knitting this document:

```{bash prepare-current-inputs, eval=FALSE}
pixi run -e default python src/notebooks/prepare_cancer_clustering_inputs.py
```

The preparation command resolves dataset participation and the
`benchmark_analysis` view through `datasets.json` helpers. It reads only
selected H5AD `obs` fields on **Bamboo**, using the configured Pixi Python,
then freezes per-sample counts and metadata locally. It does not install
cluster code, read expression matrices, submit jobs or modify canonical
artifacts. Existing H5AD checksum identities, sizes and paths are reconciled
between scratch/NAS; selected metadata receives its own digest. Full H5AD
matrix bytes are **not rehashed** in this metadata-only audit.

The legacy benchmark HiTME RDS bundles are imported with verified checksums
for comparison only. Reconciliation found count differences from current obs,
so **they are not used as the current composition input**. Exact differences
are saved with the application evidence below.

## Existing processing in ECODA

Bassez, Zhang and Pelka already have cohort-specific preprocessing,
canonical processing and automated annotation in this repository. Their
existing QC notebooks under `notebooks/QC_filtering/` and configured
benchmark-analysis views document upstream processing. In particular,
canonical Stage 3's sample-cell cutoff is upstream of this application's
additional 10-eligible-immune-cell cutoff; the latter does not replace it.

The concurrent confounding/reprocessing plan owns pipeline repair and release
work. These application snapshots record the existing processed source
identities and do not claim to be regenerated campaign outputs. Changing
author HR metadata alone does not make this application depend on author HR
labels: the application uses automated HiTME layer 2 throughout.

## Yan historical HiTME implementation

Yan is an **application-only historical import**, outside production dataset
registration. The existing aggregate bundle contains 99 samples, 27 metadata
columns, HiTME layers 1–3, and author annotation counts. Only this compact
bundle is needed locally.

The legacy workflow:

1. Read the author-distributed H5AD and use `donor_id` as sample identity;
   prepare tasks containing five samples.
2. Extract each sample from H5AD **X**, retain author `obs` metadata and create
   its Seurat object. The worker added no explicit cell-QC filter or
   `NormalizeData()` call.
3. Standardize symbols with `STACAS::StandardizeGeneSymbols`; run HiTME with
   tumor scGate models, default method parameters, seed 123 and one core.
4. Save annotated sample objects and tabulate layer 1–3 compositions.
5. Join patient and scRNA metrics supplements by `Patient_ID`/`sample`, retain
   `has_scRNA == "yes"` and annotated samples, and save `ecoda_data.rds`.

Reference filenames match ECODA's `sketched_CD8T_human_ref_v1.rds`,
`sketched_CD4T_human_ref_v2.rds`, `sketched_DC_human_ref_v2.rds`, and
`sketched_MoMac_human_v1.rds`. Historical content checksums are unavailable;
the old worker force-refreshed a scGate **dev** database. The legacy lockfile
records HiTME revision `87f8d4147aaa468438df33f50cabf2005ac518bf`, but does not
prove the exact execution runtime. Current ECODA uses validated references,
explicit normalization/counts handling and dual annotation. This import
therefore **does not claim current Pipeline 4 or scATOMIC compliance**.

Existing annotated Yan sample objects and summaries were copied directly
within NAS to `applications/cancer_clustering/imports/Yan/20261108-v1` under
the ECODA NAS project. The archive includes source scripts, the source
analysis/helper, metadata supplements and historical environment evidence.
Those lockfiles are archival evidence only and are not adopted here.
Source checksums and dirty-checkout details are in `provenance.json`;
the archive manifest MD5 is `6683d38b61426d850557afb44bc09319`.
No full H5AD or Seurat object is retained on the workstation.

# Load the frozen application inputs

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
project_root <- normalizePath(if (file.exists("datasets.json")) "." else "..", mustWork = TRUE)
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(project_root, "datasets.json")))
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)
source(file.path(project_root, "src/notebooks/ecoda_application_cancer_clustering.R"))
set.seed(42)

run_id <- "20261108-v1"
input_dir <- file.path(project_root, "data", "applications", "cancer_clustering", run_id)
result_dir <- file.path(input_dir, "derived")
plot_dir <- file.path(project_root, "plots", "ecoda_application_cancer_clustering", run_id)
dir.create(result_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(plot_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = paste0(plot_dir, "/notebook/"), dpi = 120)

application_inputs <- cancer_read_inputs(input_dir)
application <- cancer_prepare(application_inputs$inputs)
```

```{r cohort-summary}
cohort_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(application$counts), function(cohort) {
  fit <- application$pca[[cohort]]
  variance <- fit$sdev^2 / sum(fit$sdev^2)
  data.frame(cohort = cohort, samples = nrow(application$counts[[cohort]]),
    shared_types = length(application$shared_cells),
    PC1_percent = signif(100 * variance[1], 2),
    PC2_percent = signif(100 * variance[2], 2))
}))
knitr::kable(cohort_summary, row.names = FALSE)
application$shared_cells
```

```{r filtering-audit}
knitr::kable(subset(application$audit$samples, !retained), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(subset(application$audit$cell_types, reason != "retained"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Figures

The plotting call writes seven standalone PDFs with checksum sidecars. For
interactive figure iteration, rerun only the affected plotting function in
the same R session. The notebook never reruns upstream processing.

```{r make-application-figures, message=FALSE, warning=TRUE, results='hide'}
application_figures <- cancer_plot_all(application, plot_dir)
```

## Breast cancer PCA, stratification and shared axes

```{r breast-composite, fig.width=12, fig.height=14}
application_figures$plots$breast_composite
```

## Bassez shared immune composition

```{r bassez-heatmap, fig.width=11, fig.height=9}
grid::grid.newpage()
grid::grid.draw(application_figures$plots$heatmaps$Bassez$gtable)
```

## Pelka shared immune composition

Pelka uses the same shared cell types as the breast cohorts; the annotation
is MMR status. Row/column cuts are 2/2, compared with Bassez 3/3,
Yan 4/3 and Zhang 3/3.

```{r pelka-heatmap, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
grid::grid.newpage()
grid::grid.draw(application_figures$plots$heatmaps$Pelka$gtable)
```

## Cross-cohort loading correlations

Both axes are independently fitted within each cohort. The eight-axis
heatmap clusters `1 - Pearson correlation` with Ward.D2, using full-precision
correlations for clustering and rounding only the displayed fill values.

```{r cross-cohort-correlation, fig.width=6, fig.height=5}
application_figures$plots$correlation
```

## Appendix: Yan and Zhang shared immune heatmaps

```{r appendix-heatmaps, fig.width=18, fig.height=9}
application_figures$plots$appendix_heatmaps
```

# Persist traceability and numerical evidence

Application evidence is separate from canonical benchmark results. Existing
RDS evidence is checksum-verified and may be reused only when identical;
choose a new run ID for a changed input/method snapshot.

```{r persist-evidence}
source_paths <- file.path(project_root, c(
  notebook = "notebooks/ecoda_application_cancer_clustering.rmd",
  helper = "src/notebooks/ecoda_application_cancer_clustering.R",
  importer = "src/notebooks/prepare_cancer_clustering_inputs.py"
))
source_md5 <- tools::md5sum(source_paths)
stopifnot(!anyNA(source_md5))
identity <- list(run_id = run_id, source_md5 = source_md5,
  settings = application$settings, inputs = application_inputs$provenance)
cancer_save_rds(identity, file.path(result_dir, "input_and_source_identity.rds"))
cancer_save_rds(application, file.path(result_dir, "analysis.rds"))
cancer_save_rds(application_inputs$legacy_reconciliation,
  file.path(result_dir, "legacy_bundle_reconciliation.rds"))
cancer_save_rds(list(correlation = application_figures$correlation,
  clusters = application_figures$clusters,
  heatmap_matrices = application_figures$heatmap_matrices),
  file.path(result_dir, "figure_numerical_evidence.rds"))
cancer_save_rds(utils::sessionInfo(), file.path(result_dir, "session_info.rds"))
knitr::kable(data.frame(figure = names(application_figures$files),
  path = unname(application_figures$files)), row.names = FALSE)
```
